DIV8.HEAD: § 1026.19 Certain mortgage and variable-rate transactions.
DIV8.P: (a) Reverse mortgage transactions subject to RESPA—(1)(i) Time of disclosures. In a reverse mortgage transaction subject to RESPA, the creditor shall make good faith estimates of the disclosures.
(ii) Imposition of fees. Except as provided in paragraph (a)(1)(iii) of this section, neither a creditor nor any other person may impose a fee.
(2) Waiting periods for early disclosures. The disclosures must be delivered not later than the seventh business day before consummation.

(e) Mortgage loans secured by real property—Early disclosures—(1) Provision of disclosures—(i) Creditor. In a closed-end consumer credit transaction secured by real property, the creditor shall provide the consumer with good faith estimates of the disclosures.
(ii) Mortgage broker. A mortgage broker may provide the disclosures on behalf of the creditor.

(iii) Timing. Except as provided in paragraph (e)(1)(iii)(C), the creditor shall deliver or place in the mail the disclosures not later than the third business day after the creditor receives the consumer's application.
(A) The disclosures shall be delivered or placed in the mail not later than the third business day.
(B) The disclosures shall be delivered not later than the seventh business day before consummation.
DIV8.FP: This flush paragraph continues the text of paragraph (B).
DIV8.P: (f) Mortgage loans secured by real property—Final disclosures—(1) Provision of disclosures—(i) Scope. The creditor shall provide the final disclosures.
(ii) Timing. The creditor shall ensure that the consumer receives the disclosures no later than three business days before consummation.
(i) A ninth lettered paragraph, which must not be mistaken for a roman numeral.
